newsitem.title: USA: Poll shows 40 pct of Americans support Teamsters.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows 40 pct of Americans support Teamsters.

text.p: An ABC News Nightline poll indicated Tuesday that 40 percent of Americans support the Teamsters union in its strike against the United Parcel Service, which garnered only 30 percent support.
The remaining 30 percent contacted said they were neutral.

The poll, conducted by telephone Monday among a random national sample of 506 adults, also showed that while 26 percent of Americans had been inconvenienced by the nine-day-long strike, 64 percent said President Clinton should not intervene.
However, 73 percent said they personally had not been inconvenienced by the strike at the giant package delivery company and 31 percent said Clinton should halt the strike.

Seventy-nine percent of those polled said the use of part-time workers over full-time employees, a central issue in the strike, is happening more now than in the past and 57 percent said that is a "bad thing".
A majority of 68 percent said companies hire more part-timers mainly to increase profits at the expense of full-timers.

An overwhelming 82 percent said companies should be required to give part-time workers the same hourly pay as full-time employees who do similar work, while 65 percent said part-timers should get equal health insurance coverage.
